topics.title: Meaning of analysis of financial statements

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that financial analysis combines analysis (simplifying and classifying data) with interpretation (explaining its meaning and significance).
Distinguish comparison with other firms (cross-sectional analysis) from comparison with the firm's own past performance (time series analysis).

topics.title: Significance of financial analysis to its users

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the finance manager and top management use financial analysis for decisions and control.
Identify what trade payables, lenders, investors, labour unions and others look for when they analyse financial statements.

topics.title: Objectives of analysis of financial statements

concepts.learning_objective: State the objectives of financial analysis such as judging profitability, relative importance of components, reasons for change and debt-repaying ability.
Explain how economists and government use the analysis of corporate financial statements.

topics.title: Tools of analysis of financial statements

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish comparative statements (horizontal analysis) from common size statements (vertical analysis).
Calculate and interpret trend percentages with reference to a base year.
Describe the purpose of ratio analysis and cash flow analysis as tools of financial analysis.
Prepare and interpret comparative statements of profit and loss and comparative balance sheets.
Calculate absolute and percentage changes between two years in a comparative statement.
Identify the common base used in common size statements of profit and loss and balance sheets.
Calculate common size percentages and use them for intra-firm and inter-firm comparison.
Explain that financial analysis ignores price level changes and non-monetary aspects of a business.
Explain how changes in accounting policies and window dressing can make financial analysis misleading.
